raw_findings.body: hasPermission receives the Resource UUID and calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) which never matches (resource name is the group id, not the resource UUID), so it always falls back to the all-groups resource; and granted collects Resource UUIDs instead of group ids. JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery then filters user group membership by non-existent ids, returning zero users/count even though the admin has view permission on members of specific groups.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime authorization filtering silently excludes all users for group-scoped admins.
raw_findings.impact: hasPermission receives the Resource UUID and calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) which never matches (resource name is the group id, not the resource UUID), so it always falls back to the all-groups resource; and granted collects Resource UUIDs instead of group ids. JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery then filters user group membership by non-existent ids, returning zero users/count even though the admin has view permission on members of specific groups.
raw_findings.root_cause: Resource#getId() (internal resource UUID) is used where the group id (Resource#getName(), per resolveGroup) is required for both permission lookup and the returned set.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the group id, which is stored as the resource name, in both places: pass groupResource.getName() to hasPermission and add groupResource.getName() to the granted set (mirroring the V1 implementation that returns resource names).
raw_findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and evaluates the wrong resource
raw_findings.trigger: An admin whose only group access is a per-group view-members/manage-members permission (no view-users role) performs a user search or count (UsersResource.getUsersCount / searchForUser), which calls auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission().

raw_findings.body: canManage() returns true for a caller who only holds VIEW permission, allowing management operations that should require MANAGE; this is inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE and with the V1 canManage() which requires manage-users.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization check under-restricts, granting manage on view-only permission.
raw_findings.impact: canManage() returns true for a caller who only holds VIEW permission, allowing management operations that should require MANAGE; this is inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE and with the V1 canManage() which requires manage-users.
raw_findings.root_cause: The VIEW scope was included (likely copied from canView()) in the manage check.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate only the MANAGE scope in the no-arg canManage(): hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE).
raw_findings.title: canManage() grants manage capability on VIEW scope (privilege escalation)
raw_findings.trigger: An admin without the manage-users role but with only a VIEW permission on the Groups resource type calls a flow gated by GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage().

finding.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and evaluates the wrong resource
finding.trigger: An admin whose only group access is a per-group view-members/manage-members permission (no view-users role) performs a user search or count (UsersResource.getUsersCount / searchForUser), which calls auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission().
finding.verifier_reason: Patch lines 121-123 show `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. Repository context confirms `hasPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` at line 141, but resources are created with `name = resolveGroup(session, id)` (the group id) per AdminPermissionsSchema lines 109,118. So passing `groupResource.getId()` (the resource UUID) to findByName will never match a resource named by group id. The granted set then contains resource UUIDs, not group ids, causing JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery to filter by non-existent group ids.
